question.problem:
Consider the vector space ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$ of all $2\times 2$ matrices over $R.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}$ is a linearly independent set in ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
- $[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}$
- ${[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is true if and only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ So, the set is linearly independent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]=2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+(-4)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+3\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

- Statement III is false. For example, the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ can't be written as a linear combination of 

$$
{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}
$$

since all these linear combinations result in matrices with the entry ${a}_{21}=0:$

$$
a\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+b\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+c\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & c \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
